programme.title: End-Grain Cutting Board
programme.desc: Join George Vondriska to learn how to make your own end-grain cutting board that's sure to impress. Learn which types of wood work best for cutting boards and which materials to avoid when crafting anything that comes in contact with food. Find out how to properly glue, sand, and cut your pieces for a flat, even surface and achieve a finished product that is truly a cut above the rest.

programme.title: Stylish Stool
programme.desc: Create a set of stylish stools with George Vondriska's step-by-step guidance as he breaks down the construction of these attractive pieces. Learn to use your table saw to make the cuts you'll need, then see how to assemble your stool and and add decorative details for professional looking results.

programme.title: Dress Up Your Garments
programme.desc: Garments get a makeover on today's show. You can make the same pattern over and over again but it will look totally different depending on your fabric and color choice and other surface embellishments. Angela Wolf begins with a beautiful and traditional sheath dress. An intricate applique trim completely changes this basic silhouette. Then, embroidery expert Eileen Roche demonstrates simple monogram techniques for all different garments -- it's a traditional look updated with a contemporary approach.

programme.title: Cutest Projects Ever: Small Knitting, Big Impact
programme.desc: The ladies are going big by thinking small! From compact cables to cute mini skeins, this one's all about the tiny treasures that keep those needles clicking.

programme.title: Provisional Cast-On, Cable Cast-On & Split Neckline
programme.desc: Since when do knitters use crochet hooks? Find out how to work the provisional cast-on, cable cast-on, and more during the first Novel-T check in!

programme.title: Stars
programme.desc: Look beyond the sky. Jenny Barnett-Rohrs makes a glittery star catcher featuring the constellations. Candie Cooper creates a 3-D board illustrating moon phases. Artist Franz Spohn creates watercolor paintings featuring clouds. Jenny makes a suncatcher mandala and Candie Cooper captures a sparkly space galaxy in a bottle.

programme.title: Getting Started in Jewelry Making
programme.desc: With a few supplies and cold connection techniques, designer Abbi Berta quickly creates mixed media earrings. She also makes a textured cuff with a torch-fired patina to introduce metalwork. Viewer Leslie Rocha tells how her first jewelry class and love of music blossomed into a passion for making jewelry from guitar wire and picks.

programme.title: Time for Art
programme.desc: When you talk about art, we often imagine a painstaking process that takes a lot of time, but today's artists are here to show speedy techniques that still create beautiful works of art! Wyatt White starts us out with 4 projects. They are super-fast and introduce a new technique. Then Eva Sherman has tips for soldering jump rings, make a lot to start and then get creative. Tammy Honaman finishes up with ways to bring mixed media into your jewelry with resin. The process is super-fast minus the drying time.

programme.title: 3D Projects
programme.desc: Today's menu features useful 3D scrapbook projects. We make pencils with an artful touch, a scrapbook grid layout to celebrate daily life with Ali Edwards, and a scrapbook inspired tote using kaleidoscopes with Joe Rotella. Stir them all together for one fabulous Scrapbook Soup.

programme.title: Grand Opening - Proper Attire
programme.desc: Once it's built, it's time for the grand opening! Dress up with wood and clay jewelry holder from Candie Cooper. Jen Cushman stamps an on-trend metal bracelet. Rae Missigman makes a cute purse from recycled products. Mary Hettsmansperger has safety tips for working in your studio.

programme.desc: A line is an infinitely extending one-dimensional figure; one that has length but not width or thickness. In art lines are the basis that give form to a piece of art. They can be straight or curved, thick or thin, and raised or flat. Projects featuring lines: a modern art canvas with paint and masking tape; lines become three dimensional as we make a playhouse for dolls or action figures; continue with your art journal and use brightly colored pens and a special tool to make spirograph line drawings. programme.title: Crafting Cabinet Doors: Materials & Cutting Techniques
programme.desc: In the episode the craftsman guides viewers through essential techniques and considerations for crafting cabinet doors with precision and efficiency. He begins by stressing the importance of wood selection, advising against woods with prominent grain patterns like oak, which are unsuitable for door frames. Instead, he recommends using straight-grained pieces from the edges of the wood or opting for materials like MDF, birch, or maple for paint-grade projects due to their smooth surfaces and availability in large sheets. The craftsman demonstrates how to prepare materials for construction, including ripping pieces for frames and face frames, and discusses the suitability of poplar for practice due to its affordability and ease of machining. When it comes to door panels, he explains the careful use of plywood and the importance of adjusting grooves precisely for optimal fit. He showcases the use of a dado head to create tenons that snugly fit into these grooves, ensuring strong and gap-free assembly. Techniques for creating specific door styles are highlighted, such as using half-lap joints adjusted on the table saw for flush fits. The craftsman emphasizes marking and consistent cuts to avoid errors, crucial for achieving perfect joints in door frame assembly. He demonstrates assembly steps and discusses adding decorative pegs for both aesthetic appeal and structural integrity, particularly useful for heavier doors like those with leaded glass panels. Throughout the episode, the craftsman underscores the use of templates for ensuring consistent shapes, particularly useful for cathedral-style doors. He employs a band saw and router table with double-sided tape to achieve precision in shaping components, emphasizing careful setup and sequential cuts for optimal woodworking results. Overall, the episode provides comprehensive guidance on wood selection, tool adjustment, joint creation, and assembly techniques, empowering woodworkers to create high-quality cabinet doors effectively.

programme.title: Fashion Inside and Out - The Late 1940's

programme.title: Crafting Cabinet Doors: Materials & Cutting Techniques
programme.desc: In the episode the craftsman guides viewers through essential techniques and considerations for crafting cabinet doors with precision and efficiency. He begins by stressing the importance of wood selection, advising against woods with prominent grain patterns like oak, which are unsuitable for door frames. Instead, he recommends using straight-grained pieces from the edges of the wood or opting for materials like MDF, birch, or maple for paint-grade projects due to their smooth surfaces and availability in large sheets. The craftsman demonstrates how to prepare materials for construction, including ripping pieces for frames and face frames, and discusses the suitability of poplar for practice due to its affordability and ease of machining. When it comes to door panels, he explains the careful use of plywood and the importance of adjusting grooves precisely for optimal fit. He showcases the use of a dado head to create tenons that snugly fit into these grooves, ensuring strong and gap-free assembly. Techniques for creating specific door styles are highlighted, such as using half-lap joints adjusted on the table saw for flush fits. The craftsman emphasizes marking and consistent cuts to avoid errors, crucial for achieving perfect joints in door frame assembly. He demonstrates assembly steps and discusses adding decorative pegs for both aesthetic appeal and structural integrity, particularly useful for heavier doors like those with leaded glass panels. Throughout the episode, the craftsman underscores the use of templates for ensuring consistent shapes, particularly useful for cathedral-style doors. He employs a band saw and router table with double-sided tape to achieve precision in shaping components, emphasizing careful setup and sequential cuts for optimal woodworking results. Overall, the episode provides comprehensive guidance on wood selection, tool adjustment, joint creation, and assembly techniques, empowering woodworkers to create high-quality cabinet doors effectively.

programme.desc: Create custom colors and add a new twist to traditional techniques. Katie Hacker combines metals with stones and beads to make her style statement. Artist syndee holt blends polymer clay to create new colors and contemporary designs using the ancient art of mokume gane. Designer Jill MacKay shares a great die-cutting tip as she embellishes leather to make dangly earrings.

programme.title: Episode 3: Stencils
programme.desc: This show offers lots of new tips and techniques using stencils. Create your own stencil and learn about masking with Jenny Barnett Rohrs. A short interview features Stacy Julian as she shares her system of "get it done fast". Then, Julie demonstrates a layering technique using new stencil designs. Last, Julie shares more stenciling tips using stamping, painting, doodling and more.

programme.title: Friendship Stars Quilt
programme.desc: Are you Quilt Curious, but unsure where to get started? THIS is the Midnight Quilt Show episode for you!

programme.title: Quilt-As-You-Go Placemats
programme.desc: This week Angela is preparing to host a dinner for quilters, so of course, she has to quilt up a few placemats!

programme.title: Rising Star
programme.desc: Are you cut out for paper piecing? Join Angela and find out as she avoids ripping paper, her kids and chores to create a super cool rounded illusion, no curves required.

programme.title: Rail Fence
programme.desc: What happens when a rail fence meets a log cabin? Angela Walters' modern, lush batik quilt, demonstrated here!

programme.title: Craft Hacks
programme.desc: Time-saving quick tips to feed your crafting craving.

programme.desc: Learn to quilt step by step with National Quilting Circle experts on CraftsyTV.

programme.title: Artist's Academy presented by CraftsyTV
programme.desc: Welcome to Artists's Academy where we are dedicated to making you a better artist. We believe everyone has an artist within, waiting to be unleashed. Our mission is to be your ultimate resource for visual art education using tutorials covering everything from fundamental techniques to advanced concepts in painting and drawing.

programme.title: Handmade Wooden Spatula
programme.desc: The simple wooden spatula is an essential cooking tool that adds a handmade touch to any kitchen. George Vondriska demonstrates how to make your own wooden spatula in a few easy steps. This easy project makes a great gift for any home chef.

programme.title: DIY Storage Shelving System
programme.desc: Every woodworker knows the constant struggle of needing more storage space in the shop. Learn to create your own shop solutions with the help of George Vondriska. He'll show you how to make a powerhouse storage system that will give you tons of additional real estate in your shop.

programme.title: Creative Crochet Corner presented by CraftsyTV
programme.desc: Creative Crochet Corner is an online video streaming service all about learning how to crochet! Whether you're a new to crochet just learning the basics or an experienced crocheter looking for a challenge, Creative Crochet Corner is here to help. We offer a vast library of video tutorials taught by talented crochet experts who guide you through each technique step-by-step, sharing their best tips and tricks.

programme.title: Limits
programme.desc: Don't be overwhelmed interpreting designs and styles. Learn how to narrow down design choices by imposing some limits. Ebony Love shows how to limit your palette when placing color. Then, Catherine Cureton has a pieced applique technique that leaves no raw edges and uses a sewing machine. Eliane Bergmann has a lesson on seams in the machine tip. Learn how to make the perfect ¼" seam and how to stitch a partial seam.

programme.title: T-Shirt Quilt for Father's Day
programme.desc: Angela raids her husband's closet to stitch up a special quilted Father's Day gift. This T-shirt quilt for Jeremy isn't just any old T-shirt quilt; it's a very cool design that uses big flying geese to frame the blocks.

programme.title: Milky Way
programme.desc: The Walters household is eating healthy this week, but that doesn't mean Angela's quilts have to be. Today she is whipping up the Milky Way Quilt by Monique Dillard featuring Lily & Loom fabric.

programme.title: The New Millennium - the 2000's
programme.desc: As the new century dawned, fashion had gone from corsets to spandex pants in just 100 years. Even dogs were getting dressed up. Paulette Bell creates a customized dog coat using machine embroidery. Angela Wolf adds a hand warmer to work-out wear for today's trendy touch.

programme.title: Getting Started in Jewelry Making
programme.desc: With a few supplies and cold connection techniques, designer Abbi Berta quickly creates mixed media earrings. She also makes a textured cuff with a torch-fired patina to introduce metalwork. Viewer Leslie Rocha tells how her first jewelry class and love of music blossomed into a passion for making jewelry from guitar wire and picks.

programme.title: Episode 4: Technology
programme.desc: See how new machines are making their mark on your scrapbook page. Kazan Clark creates a stencil with a die cut machine and then shows how to etch on glass. Julie interviews Jenny Barnett Rohrs about how social media inspires crafting. Then, Joe Rotella uses computer software to create a snowflake Christmas ornament. Julie wraps things up with a lesson on design featuring a scrapbook page picturing family members.

programme.title: Combat Forces
programme.desc: Today, as in the past, one of the best means to enter combat is with allies. Today military forces work together to fight enemies in places such as Iraq and Afghanistan. In preparation for these deployments they constantly training with one another in joint operations. This cooperation and understanding of each other operating procedures are critical to their success in battle.

programme.title: Palliative
programme.desc: A documentary short exploring the conversations during end-of-life care with pediatric Palliative care specialist Dr. Nadia Tremonti.

programme.title: A Wing & A Prayer
programme.desc: The inspiring story of a pilot who overcame incredible odds to achieve his dream of flying solo across the Atlantic.

programme.title: All The World is Babylon
programme.desc: The documentary details the troubling political and economic realities underlying climate change by looking at the extraordinary exploitation of Arizona’s water by Saudi transnational corporations.

programme.title: Balika
programme.desc: Dipendra and Sushmita are two Napali orphans living in an orphanage in Kathmandu. One day, Dipendra's family contacts him and they invite him to travel to his hometown. Sushmita decides that when she grows up she want to be a nurse.

programme.title: Birdhill
programme.desc: Eva’s childhood home, Bratislava’s Birdhill, was once Maria Theresa's vineyards and forest. Now, cranes and excavators dominate. In her film, she meets current inhabitants, each living a different dream of this charismatic place. Yet, though they share the hill, they cannot unite to halt the ruthless, rapid construction transforming their home beyond recognition.

programme.title: Combat Forces
programme.desc: Fire and floods, the true danger at sea for sailors. At specialized training facilities, NATO sailors learn how to fight the two most common threats to any warship or submarine. From fighting fireballs to patching holes in the dark, sailors are put to the test at damage control schools. You can feel the heat, the cold and see their fear as they struggle to save their ship.

programme.title: Chasing Roo
programme.desc: An intimate portrait of wildlife rescue experts who have devoted their lives to saving kangaroos in tension with professional hunters seeking to harvest them.

programme.title: Until He's Back
programme.desc: A Moroccan family fights endless bureaucracy to recover the remains of their son Yahya, who washed up dead on a beach in Murcia in 2022, after he drowned while trying to reach Spain.

programme.title: Margin Of Error: AI, Polling and Elections
programme.desc: The goalposts are about to move in the game of public opinion polling. This film examines how a startup called Advanced Symbolics (ASI) uses artificial intelligence (AI) and social media data to forecast voter behavior.

programme.title: Fatal Flaws: Legalising Assisted Death
programme.desc: Should we be giving doctors the right to end the lives of others by euthanasia or assisted suicide? The grandfather of euthanasia in the Netherlands, Dr. Boudewijn Chabot speaks of a 'worrisome culture shift' and that euthanasia is 'getting out of hand' - especially as it relates to patients with psychiatric issues. The cost of on-going treatment is putting pressure on an already fraught decision-making process, and the many are questioning the motives of those tasked with making the decisions. Meanwhile, the suicidal can simply 'shop around' until they find the decision they are looking for, or more worryingly - others can do the same for those they are tasked with caring for.

programme.title: Women Behind The Wheel
programme.desc:
Two women. One epic journey. Countless stories that deserve to be heard. Cat and Hannah undertake a road trip across Central Asia on a mission to uncover women's stories in a region miles from their own. But along the journey, they're forced to challenge the assumptions they set out with.
Writers

programme.title: Combat Forces
programme.desc: Boarding other ships has been around since the dawn of combat at sea. Today, sailors must train to do far more than their ancestors. They must enforce embargoes, deal with pirates armed with missiles and catch smugglers. It is dangerous work. We visit some of the worlds best training facilities to understand more of what it takes to be a member of a modern Naval Boarding Party.

programme.title: Some Dogs Go To Heaven
programme.desc: The World Health Organization estimates that there are over 200 million homeless dogs in the world today. 90% of all dogs born will never find a home. This film follows CA based nonprofit Chiquita's Friends, as the team works tirelessly to confront this crisis head on.

programme.title: Built Different
programme.desc: 12-year-old Paige Calendine was born bilateral without legs.Paige has never let her disability hold her back, in fact just the opposite. She is a very successful athlete, who competes against kids who are not disabled, and wins! She even qualified for the state tournament in two sports: gymnastics and archery. The documentary is going to showcase her talent. Her inordinate determinational and courage make her Built Different.

programme.title: Undaunted, Chasing History at the Boston Marathon
programme.desc: "Undaunted: Chasing History at the Boston Marathon" is a film about the comeback of one unique runner, a 3-foot-9 physician assistant who has been mistaken for a runaway child while training. It's also about a city rallying against terror. Thousands of runners returned to compete, while a million spectators came back to cheer despite their fear. Many more around the world admired a city that wouldn't be intimidated by an attack that left hundreds wounded and three dead. "Undaunted" is also a film about every runner's fantasy: For the first half of the 2014 race, to the astonishment and sustained applause of thousands along the course, Juli led the pack.

programme.title: Temple Flavours: The Simplicity of Healing
programme.desc: A fascinating trip to Buddhist temples in South Korea. Three nuns share ancient knowledge about the truths of the contemporary world and teach that the balance of eating habits is the key to our health body, mind and the preservation of the planet.

programme.title: My Enemy, My Brother
programme.desc: My Enemy, My Brother (feature documentary) tells the true story of two former enemies who become brothers for life: Zahed Haftland was an Iranian boyu who ran away from home to join the army. Najan Aboud was a 19-year old Iraqi who had been conscripted to fight in the war, leacving behind his wife and son. Both men fought in the Iran-Iraq war where Zahed found Najah critically injured in a bunker and decided to risk his own life to save him. Because of Zahed, Bajah's was spared. Their lives diverged and they didn't see norehear of one another for 20 years,until one fateful day.

programme.title: Combat Forces
programme.desc: Boarding other ships has been around since the dawn of combat at sea. Today, sailors must train to do far more than their ancestors. They must enforce embargoes, deal with pirates armed with missiles and catch smugglers. It is dangerous work. We visit some of the worlds best training facilities to understand more of what it takes to be a member of a modern Naval Boarding Party.

programme.title: Frontline Fashion

programme.title: Smart Drugs
programme.desc: If popping a pill could make you smarter, wittier and increase your memory would you take it? If you wee a surgeon working 20 hour days and you could take a pill take kept you performing brilliantly, would you? We are on the verge of a new kind of over-the-counter drug that could change fabric of our society, they're called Nootropics, or 'smart drugs,' and they'are globally popular both at parties and in the workplace but we are only beginning to be aware of some of the side effects.

programme.title: A Punk Daydream
programme.desc: A Punk Daydream is about a group of young punks surviving on the streets of Jakarta, Indonesia’s capital. Eka and his friends have escaped parental and school authority, and strive for individual freedom amid smouldering waste. They have a dim view of Indonesia’s future which, since the end of the Suharto era, has struggled with corruption, environmental pollution and poverty. The boys’ (facial) tattoos both symbolise and create their break with society, as they have a stigmatising effect. Tattoo bearers are assumed to be criminals and can hardly find work. The punks feel kinship with the Dayak people, who have traditional tattoos and try to cling to their centuries-old lifestyle, knowing full well their culture will ultimately disappear: along with the rain forest. The filmmakers ingeniously intertwine documentary, video art and photography with fairy-tale traditions and contemporary reality. Eka hopes to reconnect to society by acting out his own story in the film. (International Film Festival Rotterdam)

programme.title: Far Away From Home
programme.desc: A group of children and adolescents, from different Latin American countries are living in shelters in Tijuana. They are all waiting for a response to their request for asylum to enter the USA. The wait is long and uncertain, they are childhoods on hold.

programme.title: The Internet of Everything
programme.desc: The Internet is invading all aspects of your life. No longer confined to your computer or your phone, the Internet is now in garbage cans, refrigerators, and the infrastructure of our cities. With the connecting of the physical world into the "Internet of Things", the stakes have been raised - it's no longer just the abstractions of cyberspace that are spinning out of control, but instead our homes, our bodies and our cities that are being transfrormed. The future will either be a surveillance nightnmare or an eco-utopia, the outcome determined by start ups in Silicon Valley and Shenzhen.

programme.title: Dying For A Smoke
programme.desc: In an age where smoking is becoming increasingly frowned upon, banned and distasteful, there’s one sector of the New Zealand community where evidence suggests the message isn’t getting through fast enough: 31% of Maori deaths are due to cigarette smoking 46% of Maori are regular smokers compared to 21% of non-Maori Dying For A Smoke is an in-depth investigation into New Zealand’s smoking problem, specifically focusing on smoking among Maori but also looking at trends within the wider community. programme.title: Combat Forces
programme.desc: Artillery is known as the hammer of the battlefield because of the awesome firepower it can bring down on an enemy. Imagine if that same firepower could be mobile and dropped behind enemy lines? That is the premise behind airborne artillery, a specialized force charged with supporting soldiers with long distance firepower. We go to Fort Bragg NC to learn about this unique warfare discipline.

programme.title: Conducting Life
programme.desc: Filmed over seven years, the film follows the improbable journey of conductor Roderick Cox and his quest to succeed in the highly competitive field of orchestral conducting. This profession has traditionally overlooked musicians of color.

programme.desc: Frontline Fashion is an award-winning docu-series that follows the most talented emerging fashion designers from all over the globe

programme.title: The Power of Play
programme.desc: Lizards do it. Even fish do it. The animal world is showing us why play is a serious matter. Through a combination of ongoing experiments, reconstructed experiments and guided observation. The Power of Play reveals surprising truths about play in the natural world. Scientists from Europe, the United States and Canada, many of them pioneers in the field, offer convincing evidence that play is not to be taken lightly. In fact, it has the power to make animals and humans smarter, healthier and more likely to survive.

programme.title: Fight Club London
programme.desc: Fight Club London looks at one of the world's fastest growing sports, Mixed Martial Arts. Three fighters prepare for upcoming cage fights. A 14 year boy, a fully-fledged pro, and an Indian girl who wants to make her cage debut before she gets married. What’s the true reality behind this sport?

programme.title: Who Made You?
programme.desc: Artificial intellignce is reaching our mental and physical existence like never before. The film leads us to the world of cyborgs, sex robots and androids. It challenges us to face our values, ethics and rethink our position. To keep our humanistic values on board with the development, we have to be awake - tight now. Eye-opening scences from Finland, Spain, Swedenm Geece amd Japan reveals the on-going processes and development on a global level. The guide in our stimulating journey is a young aspiring Dr Michael Laakasuo who is making pioneering research on the field of ethics and AI. He stresses that machine-ethics should not be left behind in the technological development. The film asks what the development of AI means to us as human beings. What does it mean for humanity, community, and how it will affect our perception of human? What are the values we want to hold on to?

A 14 year boy, a fully-fledged pro, and an Indian girl who wants to make her cage debut before she gets married. What’s the true reality behind this sport?

programme.title: Who Made You?
programme.desc: Artificial intellignce is reaching our mental and physical existence like never before. The film leads us to the world of cyborgs, sex robots and androids. It challenges us to face our values, ethics and rethink our position. To keep our humanistic values on board with the development, we have to be awake - tight now. Eye-opening scences from Finland, Spain, Swedenm Geece amd Japan reveals the on-going processes and development on a global level. The guide in our stimulating journey is a young aspiring Dr Michael Laakasuo who is making pioneering research on the field of ethics and AI. He stresses that machine-ethics should not be left behind in the technological development. The film asks what the development of AI means to us as human beings. What does it mean for humanity, community, and how it will affect our perception of human? What are the values we want to hold on to?

programme.title: Combat Forces
programme.desc: Artillery is known as the hammer of the battlefield because of the awesome firepower it can bring down on an enemy. Imagine if that same firepower could be mobile and dropped behind enemy lines? That is the premise behind airborne artillery, a specialized force charged with supporting soldiers with long distance firepower. We go to Fort Bragg NC to learn about this unique warfare discipline.

programme.title: Conducting Life
programme.desc: Filmed over seven years, the film follows the improbable journey of conductor Roderick Cox and his quest to succeed in the highly competitive field of orchestral conducting. This profession has traditionally overlooked musicians of color.

programme.title: Frontline Fashion
programme.desc: Frontline Fashion is an award-winning docu-series that follows the most talented emerging fashion designers from all over the globe

programme.title: The Power of Play
programme.desc: Lizards do it. Even fish do it. The animal world is showing us why play is a serious matter. Through a combination of ongoing experiments, reconstructed experiments and guided observation. The Power of Play reveals surprising truths about play in the natural world. Scientists from Europe, the United States and Canada, many of them pioneers in the field, offer convincing evidence that play is not to be taken lightly. In fact, it has the power to make animals and humans smarter, healthier and more likely to survive.

programme.title: Tent City Hollywood
programme.desc: Explore Hollywood's streets over 9 months-unchanged struggles, untold stories. A raw look at the encampments in Los Angeles.

programme.title: 24 Hours At Gound Zero
programme.desc: An extraordinary inside look at the evolution of the World Trade Center horror, experienced through the eyes and the voices of people at the scene including a policeman, a fireman and an EMS worker who were among the first to arrive at ground zero. Our cameras wer the first on hand and we have some of the most definitive footage from the event of its time. This program aired on MSNBC.

programme.title: Town Of Glory
programme.desc: As Russia faces growing international isolation, loyalists within the 30 million-strong Russian diaspora are dedicated to defending, supporting and promoting Putin overseas. Vladimir Putin has made it clear that he wants Russia to reclaim its former glory: across the globe.

programme.title: Gun Shot Wound
programme.desc: Gun Shot Wound takes a hard look at routine gun violence in America through the eyes of its trauma surgeons. The film examines the crisis through a public health lens and highlights hospital-based violence intervention programs designed to combat the epidemic. Every day in the United States, an average of 318 people are shot - about 116,000 victims each year. Most aren't involved in mass shootings, instead they're caught in the web of routine, almost invisioble, gun violence. Gun Shot Wound show what really happens when someone gets shot and highlights how physicians and hospitals are not just treating patients, but going above and beyond to prevent gun violence.

programme.title: The House In Arguello
programme.desc: Valentina Llorens’ uncle disappeared during the military dictatorship in Argentina. When his remains are discovered she starts researching the family’s history. Her grandmother was active in the civil movement “Mothers of Plaza de Mayo” and her mother political prisoner.

programme.title: Combat Forces
programme.desc: Today, as in the past, one of the best means to enter combat is with allies. Today military forces work together to fight enemies in places such as Iraq and Afghanistan. In preparation for these deployments they constantly training with one another in joint operations. This cooperation and understanding of each other operating procedures are critical to their success in battle.

programme.title: All The World is Babylon
programme.desc: The documentary details the troubling political and economic realities underlying climate change by looking at the extraordinary exploitation of Arizona’s water by Saudi transnational corporations.

programme.title: Balika
programme.desc: Dipendra and Sushmita are two Napali orphans living in an orphanage in Kathmandu. One day, Dipendra's family contacts him and they invite him to travel to his hometown. Sushmita decides that when she grows up she want to be a nurse.

programme.title: Birdhill
programme.desc: Eva’s childhood home, Bratislava’s Birdhill, was once Maria Theresa's vineyards and forest. Now, cranes and excavators dominate. In her film, she meets current inhabitants, each living a different dream of this charismatic place. Yet, though they share the hill, they cannot unite to halt the ruthless, rapid construction transforming their home beyond recognition.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: Discover China is a documentary series shot in conjunction with the Chinese Ministry of Culture and China Central Television, including footage of never before seen locations and recreations of historical events. It was shot by BBC film crews over a four year period. At the foot of Tai Mountain sits an enigma, a temple that bears a striking resemblance to an Imperial palace. It was built by a brazen emperor, who ignored his country's desparation, and built this lavish shrine to bolster his status as the sole ruler.

programme.title: MOMA - Moments of Modern Art
programme.desc: Moments of Modern Art is a special feature, showcasing incredible works of art and design. From sculptures to tattoos, photography to smartphone art, learn what inspires artists and designers, have a glance into the world of contemporary art and be uplifted by the dedication they have to their craft. With stories from all over the world, this is more than a show about art and design; this is a way of living!

programme.title: Haunted New Orleans
programme.desc: In the heart of the Big Easy, restless spirits reveal chilling tales-voodoo curses, spectral jazz, and forgotten secrets. Ghosts, cryptids, and eerie history explore the supernatural secrets of New Orleans in this chilling documentary.

programme.title: State of Rodeo
programme.desc: State of Rodeo follows a diverse group of characters who participate in the sport of rodeo and explores the heritage of the cattle industry within the state of Florida and it's influence on western culture from the time of Ponce De Leon's first settlement to present day cowboys and cowgirls. Rodeo still fascinates to this day, the heritage of this sport's tradition is one of the founding industries of our nation and most people don't know that Florida played an integral role in this history.

programme.title: In The Executioner's Shadow
programme.desc: The death penalty is one of America's most polarizing practices. Meet an executioner, a bombing victim struggling with justice, and parents whose child was murdered, in this doc, exploring capital punishment.

programme.title: We Don’t Do Charity
programme.desc: Across the Global South social entrepreneurs, civil society organisations, and grass roots NGOs are rejecting the ‘white saviourism’ of rich countries in favour of sustainable development programmes designed by them, for their own communities.

programme.title: Meherio

programme.title: A Gallery Without Walls
programme.desc: In a secluded spot at the eastern end of New Zealand's Waiheke Island lies Connells Bay where John and Jo Gow, passionate and well-known in art and sculpture circles have established the Connells Bay Sculpture Park where art and nature are united to create special spaces for site specific sculpture.

programme.title: Jaffa: A Guide to Gentrification
programme.desc: Jaffa, once a major port in the Middle East and the sister city of Tel Aviv, “the most expensive city in the world” per The Economist, has grown into an international tourist center, a coveted destination and last but not least a true real estate gem.

programme.title: On The Inside Of a Military Dictatorship
programme.desc:
“On the Inside of a Military Dictatorship” takes its audience back to when the military made their master plan for a so-called disciplined democracy in Myanmar and wrote a very scripted role for their enemy no. 1; Aung San Suu Kyi. In a dramatic way, the film builds the character- and story set-up to take us anew into the crisis we know from the news – however, with a radically different perspective. The story is based on unique acces to the key players in this complicated reality, including Aung San Suu Kyi and previous President Thein Sein.
It’s the story of how power struggles unfold and how political enemies can end up being closer than the ones they claim to fight for: the people. The audience gets deeper and deeper into this complex world of power driven by peculiar characters and even astrology.

programme.desc: Jaffa, once a major port in the Middle East and the sister city of Tel Aviv, “the most expensive city in the world” per The Economist, has grown into an international tourist center, a coveted destination and last but not least a true real estate gem.

programme.title: On The Inside Of a Military Dictatorship
programme.desc:
“On the Inside of a Military Dictatorship” takes its audience back to when the military made their master plan for a so-called disciplined democracy in Myanmar and wrote a very scripted role for their enemy no. 1; Aung San Suu Kyi. In a dramatic way, the film builds the character- and story set-up to take us anew into the crisis we know from the news – however, with a radically different perspective. The story is based on unique acces to the key players in this complicated reality, including Aung San Suu Kyi and previous President Thein Sein.
It’s the story of how power struggles unfold and how political enemies can end up being closer than the ones they claim to fight for: the people. The audience gets deeper and deeper into this complex world of power driven by peculiar characters and even astrology.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: Discover China is a documentary series shot in conjunction with the Chinese Ministry of Culture and China Central Television, including footage of never before seen locations and recreations of historical events. It was shot by BBC film crews over a four year period. At the foot of Tai Mountain sits an enigma, a temple that bears a striking resemblance to an Imperial palace. It was built by a brazen emperor, who ignored his country's desparation, and built this lavish shrine to bolster his status as the sole ruler.

programme.title: MOMA - Moments of Modern Art
programme.desc: Moments of Modern Art is a special feature, showcasing incredible works of art and design. From sculptures to tattoos, photography to smartphone art, learn what inspires artists and designers, have a glance into the world of contemporary art and be uplifted by the dedication they have to their craft. With stories from all over the world, this is more than a show about art and design; this is a way of living!

programme.title: The Loop
programme.desc: A small discovery leads two adventurers to climb the cliffs of their home island and make unexpected discoveries. Their challenge, obstructed by tons of pollution that is swept up the coast every day, marks a shift in perspective and their interaction with our environment.

programme.title: Desert Coffee
programme.desc: Slab City is a squatter community in the Sonoran Desert and 'the last free place in America'. The inhabitants live off-the-grid in broken trailers or old school buses with no running water, electricity or sewage system. Their closest neighbours are the Marine Corps, who practice aerial bombing in the area.

programme.title: The Negotiators How To Make Peace
programme.desc: Featuring an inquisitive look at the identity and evolution of those people who seek solutions to armed conflicts in the 21st century.Negotiators talk about their work, their evaluation of the situations, and also the personal cost to them.

It's More Fun in the Philippines
programme.desc: After a morning visiting some of the indigenous communities, to learn their traditional skills, Liü and Mel have an amazing welcome from a mayor, and cross to a new island for a cycling adventure.

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Alyse Edwards continues her journey in the Turkish town of Alacati. Starting inland she explores some of the remains of ancient civilisations and experiences some incredible views of Alacati and the surrounding areas. After a brief stop off for some exquisite wine, she heads to the nearby coastal town of Cesme for some further exploring and puts herself to the test by having a go at the famous local sport of Wind Surfing.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: In the remote, ancient villages of southern Anhui Province in southeast China, a breed of merchants emerged, altering and reshaping the face of China’s trade and commerce. Cast in to the tumultuous world of business at a tender, early age, these boys turned into some of China’s most successful traders, businessmen and merchants. With their legacy firmly secure in their centuries old lavish and opulent houses, and their illustrious careers recorded in the annals of history for posterity, these shrewd astute, and influential merchants helped shape China’s commercial past for centuries. Discover China follows in the footsteps of the famous Huizhou Merchants.

programme.desc: Continuing her journey through the Black Forest, Liu has to catch and forage for her dinner, and has a wine tasting in a cellar where they used to hold witch trials.

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Doused in heritage with old hamlets, drowsy villages and towns studding its lush green hills, Southern France’s Occitania region only officially come into being in 2016 with the pairing of Languedoc-Roussillon and the Midi-Pyrenees. The two historically Occitan regions are blessed with colour, tranquility, and a wealth of UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Food and drink are still approached with reverence in the region, and a whistle stop tour around four different departments of the Midi Pyrenees; Tarn, Gers, Tarn-et-Garonne and Haute Garonne gives you plenty of opportunity to experience some of its best gastronomy, as Katy Dartford discovers.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: Located on the ancient Silk Road, Dunhuang Oasis was the epicenter of an amazing discovery at the turn of the century. Taoist monk Wang Yuan Lu, who was appointed to care for a Buddhist holy place, was displeased with his position. A fateful sweep of the broom revealed a secret cache of thousands of Buddhist scrolls, unlocking the secrets held within the Sutra Cave. Over 50,000 artifacts, murals, statues, idols spanning the history of 12 different Chinese Dynasties were discovered. News of the find led to the discovery of the Mogao Grottoes by a British explorer who was surveying the ruins in the area. Fascinated by the find, Sir Marc Aurel Stein led the first of several foreign expeditions who bargained with the monk for these priceless artifacts, leaving the Mogao Grottos nearly empty. To this day, China is still heart broken at the loss.

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Join John Plaskett as he heads deep into the Pyrenees Mountains in Catalonia. Normally a popular destination during the winter months we thought we’d check it out during the summer. Experience the amazing views as John hikes through national parks and beautiful gorges. But it’s not just a place for trekking as he also experiences cycling on part of the Tour de France route and enjoys the thrills of white-water rafting.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: An age old sketching of plans for an imperial garden design drew the attention of two prominent Chinese architectural scholars. Upon further examination, they were shocked to discover he sketch’s true origins and exactly what the blueprints depicted. In their quest for more information, they unraveled the secret methods of construction for the world’s largest palace complex: The Forbidden City. From the blueprints, to small scale models, to the ingenious construction solutions conceived which brought a family, generations of success and wealth. Discover China delves into the foundations of how this impressive palace is constructed and provide detailed examination of Imperial Architectural Designs.

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Join Ellen Coughlan as she explores the iconic city of New Orleans. Nicknamed the “Big Easy”, it’s known for its round the clock nightlife, vibrant live-music scene, and a spicy, singular cuisine… reflecting its history as a melting pot of French, African and American cultures. New Orleans is famous for its Mardi Gras, where parades and street parties fill the city. It’s also home to the iconic Natchez Steamboat, the last completely steam powered paddleboat on the Mississippi River.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: This ancient city, once threatened by the teeth of modern development, stands proud as one of China’s defining economical centers, and one of the few to retain their original visage. The institutions honed and developed in this ancient city have long been lost, but the city’s remarkable architecture and history remain very much intact. The pioneers of the Chinese financial system came from this city, making their marks in every corner of the country. Their influence swelled well beyond the thick city walls, leaving behind an impressive legacy of commerce, finance and business. Discover China, as we unlock the vault containing the valuable secrets of Ancient Pingyao.

programme.title: Hiking Europe-The alpe Adria Tail
programme.desc: Starting in Austria, Esme Todd begins her long, 750km hike along the Alpe Adria Trail. From farms to hunting for gold, Esme has an unforgettable start to her journey. And then there are the amazing waterfalls!!

programme.title: The Boat Show

programme.title: The Flying Chef
programme.desc: The Island of Alor is a place where coastal fishing villages trade seafood for meat, fruit and vegetables from the farming villages. Chef Nathan prepares fresh tuna sashimi.

programme.title: Escape To Paradise
programme.desc: The Caribbean has always been a dream destination for holidaymakers dreaming of that perfect getaway, and Antigua has long been a favourite for the British. Of course, it spent several centuries under British rule, and the connections endure in names such as Nelson’s Dockyard and English Harbour. Today though, it’s the 365 beaches, year round sunshine, and colourful cocktails that bring the visitors.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: A forbidden city that was built hundreds of miles away from the capital in Beijing, still stands today on the hills and crests of this mountain, its peak serves as a ladder to heaven. The mysteries of this now deserted structure, which served both a ruler and a deity, are slowly being revealed. Wudang Mountain stands, aloof, veiled in mysterious tales of ancient gods and rich in imperial history. Its ridges stretch, shrouded with clouds and mist all year round. Discover China brings you the Mystery of XuanWu, a riveting tale of the bond between an emperor and a god, the link between man and nature, and the story behind WuDang Mountain, and its mystifying peaks.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: No one could have dreamed that beneath the fields of a slumbering village in Henan province, a dormant civilization was awaiting to be brought back to light. From the discovery of mysteriously etched and engraved bone fragments and tortoise shells, an age old era of China emerged from beneath the plowed fields. As archeological excavations began, an age old fear of grave robbers set in the surveyor’s heart , when the wall of an ancient tomb was finally exposed. As the arduous explorations continued, an age in China’s history was finally uncovered. Discover China unearths the secrets of the Underground City.

Starting inland she explores some of the remains of ancient civilisations and experiences some incredible views of Alacati and the surrounding areas. After a brief stop off for some exquisite wine, she heads to the nearby coastal town of Cesme for some further exploring and puts herself to the test by having a go at the famous local sport of Wind Surfing.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: In the remote, ancient villages of southern Anhui Province in southeast China, a breed of merchants emerged, altering and reshaping the face of China’s trade and commerce. Cast in to the tumultuous world of business at a tender, early age, these boys turned into some of China’s most successful traders, businessmen and merchants. With their legacy firmly secure in their centuries old lavish and opulent houses, and their illustrious careers recorded in the annals of history for posterity, these shrewd astute, and influential merchants helped shape China’s commercial past for centuries. Discover China follows in the footsteps of the famous Huizhou Merchants.

programme.title: Essence Of India
programme.desc:
Samira is all excited for the Tandoori Party.
The world loves to BBQ and India has some of the oldest forms – Tandoori cooking. Samira takes a fresh approach to Tandoori cuisine and the grill that goes back thousands of years.
The Episode starts off with a visit to a Street Tandoori hub that makes Kababs that have a cult following of their own. Samira ends up taking over grill, learns the art of Tandoori breads and how can any Tandoori feast be complete without the Pièce de résistance, The Tandoori Chicken and a Party!

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Join Ellen Coughlan as she explores the iconic city of New Orleans. Nicknamed the “Big Easy”, it’s known for its round the clock nightlife, vibrant live-music scene, and a spicy, singular cuisine… reflecting its history as a melting pot of French, African and American cultures. New Orleans is famous for its Mardi Gras, where parades and street parties fill the city. It’s also home to the iconic Natchez Steamboat, the last completely steam powered paddleboat on the Mississippi River. The second part features more food, some cocktail making and a voyage on the beautiful Natchez.

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Join Ellen Coughlan as she explores the iconic city of New Orleans. Nicknamed the “Big Easy”, it’s known for its round the clock nightlife, vibrant live-music scene, and a spicy, singular cuisine… reflecting its history as a melting pot of French, African and American cultures. New Orleans is famous for its Mardi Gras, where parades and street parties fill the city. It’s also home to the iconic Natchez Steamboat, the last completely steam powered paddleboat on the Mississippi River. The second part features more food, some cocktail making and a voyage on the beautiful Natchez.

programme.title: Angie Gensler
programme.desc: News - Angie Gensler is a mother and personal trainer who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2004. In this episode, Mathew Embry speaks with Angie about her diagnosis and why she ultimately chose not to pursue drug treatments. Instead, she focused on lifestyle changes including diet, exercise, and daily discipline. Along the way she faced several major challenges including a serious car accident, a hysterectomy, and the effects of menopause, all while continuing to pursue optimal health and eventually stepping onto the competitive bodybuilding stage in her 50s. Her story is an inspiration to anyone navigating a difficult diagnosis.

programme.title: Angie Gensler
programme.desc: News - Angie Gensler is a mother and personal trainer who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2004. In this episode, Mathew Embry speaks with Angie about her diagnosis and why she ultimately chose not to pursue drug treatments. Instead, she focused on lifestyle changes including diet, exercise, and daily discipline. Along the way she faced several major challenges including a serious car accident, a hysterectomy, and the effects of menopause, all while continuing to pursue optimal health and eventually stepping onto the competitive bodybuilding stage in her 50s. Her story is an inspiration to anyone navigating a difficult diagnosis.

programme.title: Trevor Wicken
programme.desc: News - Movement may be one of the most powerful tools available for people living with multiple sclerosis. In this episode of Hope & Health, Mathew Embry speaks with Trevor Wicken, founder of The MS Gym, about how targeted movement training can help people with MS improve mobility, strength, and neurological function. The conversation explores neuroplasticity, foot drop, and the discipline required to stay consistent with movement when living with a neurological condition. Trevor also shares how a spinal injury at 16 shaped his philosophy and how two women living with MS ultimately changed the direction of his career and led to the creation of The MS Gym

programme.title: Trevor Wicken
programme.desc: News - Movement may be one of the most powerful tools available for people living with multiple sclerosis. In this episode of Hope & Health, Mathew Embry speaks with Trevor Wicken, founder of The MS Gym, about how targeted movement training can help people with MS improve mobility, strength, and neurological function. The conversation explores neuroplasticity, foot drop, and the discipline required to stay consistent with movement when living with a neurological condition. Trevor also shares how a spinal injury at 16 shaped his philosophy and how two women living with MS ultimately changed the direction of his career and led to the creation of The MS Gym

programme.title: Survive the Wild - S01:E01 - Rules of the Realm
programme.desc: Animals or groups protect their territory by using sounds like birds singing or scents like pheromones from many mammals to mark boundaries. These are just the initial warnings. If other animals ignore these signs, a conflict might happen. Animals need a secure territory to mate, raise their young, and ensure there's enough food and resources for survival. This episode looks at the strategies animals use to claim their territory.

programme.title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E42 - Diana A Model Princess
programme.desc: Diana's fashion sense was something people often looked at closely. She had a knack for picking outfits that were both stylish and sophisticated, which always grabbed attention. Her hair was also iconic, usually styled neatly with a slight bounce, perfectly framing her face and adding to her elegant appearance.
programme.sub-title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E42 - Diana A Model Princess

programme.title: Dropped - S05:E01 - Empty Handed
programme.desc: In remote areas, survival is an everyday game. Enter hosts Chris and Casey Keefer as they set out to survive 30 days in the backcountry. Each new day these brothers will pit their skills as hunters, woodsmen, and fishermen against an unforgiving and relentless landscape. DROPPED brings viewers face to face with the harsh reality of only being able to eat what you can kill. A true test of survival. The Keefer brothers put boots to ground as their journey through Alaska begins. Armed with nothing but a couple Glock 20s, the brothers immediately begin their search for their first supply-yielding catch.

programme.title: Dropped - S05:E02 - Long Days, Cold Nights
programme.desc: The Keefer brothers awaken to a frozen tundra. With over 8 miles to cover and no oars, the brothers are forced to trudge their way through shallow water and barren earth as they head downstream in search of their second cache.
programme.sub-title: Dropped - S05:E02 - Long Days, Cold Nights

programme.title: Wardens - S03:E12 - Operation White Sulpher
programme.desc: Wardens are sorting through some hunters' conflicting tales, causing a guy to get in a bit of a jam. At the same time, other wardens are handling people trying to sneak onto properties as hunting season wraps up.

programme.title: Survive the Wild - S01:E02 - Nature's World Wide Web
programme.desc: When animals share info to help each other decide, it's called animal communication. They use stuff like sounds, colors, body language, movements, electric signs, touches, smells, or a mix of these. Whether it's a sea anemone spreading its tentacles or a male lion considering approaching a mate, their skill in communicating can be vital for their success. This episode dives into how animals interact with one another.
programme.sub-title: Survive the Wild - S01:E02 - Nature's World Wide Web

programme.sub-title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E01 - Diana A Portrait

programme.title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E02 - The Fergie Story Paradise Lost

programme.sub-title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E02 - The Fergie Story Paradise Lost

programme.title: Dropped - S05:E03 - Choke Point

programme.title: Dropped - S05:E04 - Bone Weary
programme.desc: The Keefer brothers take shelter in a small pine outcropping as a winter storm sets siege to the river. Forced to wait out the arctic blast, the brothers try and retain what little energy they have left.

programme.title: Wardens - S04:E01 - Antler Raiders
programme.desc: Montana game wardens try to control the masses as the gates open and antler hunters are set free to find their trophies.

programme.title: Wardens - S04:E02 - Across The Seeded Fields
programme.desc: Montana game wardens are out on the first day of pronghorn season, keeping an eye on both lawful and unlawful hunting, and making sure seeded fields don't get damaged.
programme.sub-title: Wardens - S04:E02 - Across The Seeded Fields

programme.title: Survive the Wild - S01:E03 - Cunning Copulation
programme.desc: Finding a mate, building a nest, and raising kids are all part of the whole reproductive behavior thing. But it’s not as easy as it sounds. First, you’ve got to sift through lots of possible partners to find the one with the best genes to keep your family line going. Nesting involves finding some space and then guarding it fiercely, while raising the little ones takes loads of energy as you have to feed, teach, and keep them safe until they grow up. This episode dives into the ins and outs of how creatures go about their reproductive business.
programme.sub-title: Survive the Wild - S01:E03 - Cunning Copulation

programme.title: Wardens Case Files - S01:E09 - Operation Bruin and Peanut Road
programme.desc: Game Wardens dive into a challenging case with 'Operation Bruin'. Later, they share a funny tale about a decoy deer mishap in 'Peanut Road'. Wardens also reminisce about memorable investigations from their experiences.
programme.sub-title: Wardens Case Files - S01:E09 - Operation Bruin and Peanut Road

programme.title: Wardens Case Files - S01:E10 - Strange Killings and Dog Help
programme.desc: In "Strange Killings," you'll hear about an incredible tale of chaos out in the wilderness. Then, in "Dog Help," a trusty dog lends a hand to a Game Warden. Game Wardens share some of the most memorable cases and stories from their careers.
programme.sub-title: Wardens Case Files - S01:E10 - Strange Killings and Dog Help

programme.sub-title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E04 - Elizabeth At 80 Continuity And Change

programme.title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E43 - Diana A Day In The Life
programme.desc: When Diana got engaged, she was constantly in the media's eyes. Throughout her life, she focused on her sons and committed herself to charity work, like speaking out against land mines. Diana used her fame to bring attention to this and other important issues. This well-researched show takes a closer look at one of the 20th century's most amazing people. With never-before-seen footage, it shows her path from a shy teen to becoming the beloved Diana, Princess of Wales, including touching moments from her last days.
programme.sub-title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E43 - Diana A Day In The Life

programme.title: Survive the Wild - S01:E04 - Battle Plans
programme.desc: Surviving in the wild often means being able to fight and win. This fighting strategy is called agonism and is used to set ranks, get resources, claim territory, and attract partners. programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E05 - Strongest
programme.desc: How do you decide which is the strongest animal on the Planet? Wild Ones looks at the comparative strength of the tiniest of ants to that of a might grizzly bear, or a deadly crocodile to the indestructible rhinoceros.

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E06 - Cutest
programme.desc: The charming kangaroo. The cuddly koala. The beautiful butterfly. The cheerful clownfish. Or the adorable budgie - which one is the cutest of them all?

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E07 - Wild Australia
programme.desc: More than 80 percent of Australia’s plants, mammals, reptiles and frogs are unique to Australia and are found nowhere else in the world. Wild dingos, frisky kangaroos, deceptively cuddly looking koalas and playful platypuses are some of the most iconic of Australia’s wild animals.

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E08 - Masters of the Sky
programme.desc: So many words describe the many ways that birds fly – pelicans and kestrels soar but owls fly silently. Parrots flock, vultures swarm and eagles swoop. Radar-accurate eyes scan the ground and slotted feathers adjust flight paths as hawks attack. But, which is the true master of the sky?
programme.sub-title: Wild Ones - S01:E08 - Masters of the Sky

programme.desc: How do you decide which is the strongest animal on the Planet? Wild Ones looks at the comparative strength of the tiniest of ants to that of a might grizzly bear, or a deadly crocodile to the indestructible rhinoceros.

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E06 - Cutest
programme.desc: The charming kangaroo. The cuddly koala. The beautiful butterfly. The cheerful clownfish. Or the adorable budgie - which one is the cutest of them all?

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E07 - Wild Australia
programme.desc: More than 80 percent of Australia’s plants, mammals, reptiles and frogs are unique to Australia and are found nowhere else in the world. Wild dingos, frisky kangaroos, deceptively cuddly looking koalas and playful platypuses are some of the most iconic of Australia’s wild animals.

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E08 - Masters of the Sky
programme.desc: So many words describe the many ways that birds fly – pelicans and kestrels soar but owls fly silently. Parrots flock, vultures swarm and eagles swoop. Radar-accurate eyes scan the ground and slotted feathers adjust flight paths as hawks attack. But, which is the true master of the sky?
